title: Regular ring maps are stable under finite type base change
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to\Lambda$ be a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] of commutative rings (flat, with every fibre ring $\Lambda\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$), and let $R\to R'$ be a ring map of finite type, i.e. $R'$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Then the base change $R'\to\Lambda\otimes_RR'$, $r'\mapsto1\otimes r'$, is a regular ring map. (Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C1.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07C1 (lemma-regular-base-change, 'Regular maps and base change'), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07C1; its proof uses Algebra lemma-flat-base-change, lemma-Noetherian-field-extension and lemma-geometrically-regular. Used in the proof of Proposition 07PV ('as a localization of a base change of the regular ring map R -> R^').
